It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. Today, it is an extramural subsidiary shrine of {{ill|Kamayama Shrine|fr|Sanctuaire Kamayama|ja|竈山神社|simple|Kamayama Shrine|qid=Q11597743}}. {{nihongo|'''Shizuhi Shrine'''|静火神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Kii Province|cs|Provincie Kii|de|Provinz Kii|es|Provincia de Kii|eu|Kii probintzia|fa|ولایت کیئی|fr|Province de Kii|gl|Provincia de Kii|id|Provinsi Kii|it|Kii (provincia)|ja|紀伊国|ko|기이국|lt|Kijo žemė|nl|Kii (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Kii|pt|Província de Kii|ru|Кии (провинция)|simple|Kii Province|sk|Kii (provincia)|sr|Провинција Киј|th|แคว้นคิอิ|tr|Kii (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кії|vi|Tỉnh Kii|zh|紀伊國|zh_min_nan|Kii-kok|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province}}.

Together with {{ill|Itate Shrine|ja|伊達神社 (和歌山市)|qid=Q11380847|lt=Date Shrine}} (Sonobe, Wakayama City) and {{ill|Shima Shrine|ja|志磨神社|zh|志磨神社|qid=Q17212913}} ({{ill|Nakanoshima|ja|中之島 (和歌山市)|qid=Q17226981|lt=Nakanoshima}}, Wakayama City), it is known as the “Ki Sansho-sha” (Three Shrines of Ki) {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine Site (Heibonsha)|1983|p=376}}.

== Enshrined deity ==
The enshrined deity is the following single kami {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987|p=99}}:
:* Shizuhi Ōkami

According to documents of the Ugai clan, the shrine’s hereditary priests, the deity was identified as {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|az|Kaqutsuçi|de|Kagutsuchi|es|Kagutsuchi|fa|کاگو-تسوچی|fr|Kagutsuchi|it|Kagutsuchi|ja|カグツチ|mni|ꯀꯒꯨ-ꯁꯨꯆꯤ|pl|Kagutsuchi|ru|Кагуцути|sv|Kagutsuchi|ta|ககுட்சூசி|tr|Kagutsuchi|uk|Кагу-цуті|zh|迦具土|qid=Q1640658|lt=Hi-no-Musubi no Kami}} {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987|p=99}}. Another theory, found in the *Zoku Fudoki*, holds that the “Ki Sansho-sha” were branch enshrinements of the three deities of Isonokami—Itsu no Take no Mikoto, Ōyatsuhime no Mikoto, and Tsumatsuhime no Mikoto—and identifies the deity of Shizuhi Shrine as Tsumatsuhime no Mikoto {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine Site (Heibonsha)|1983|p=376}}. Yet another view considers Shizuhi to have been a “fire-quelling deity” of Kii Province, known as the “Land of Trees” {{Sfn|Kamayama Shrine and Shizuhi Shrine (Kami-gami)|1986|pp=316–318}}. In addition, the *{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|ja|住吉大社神代記|qid=Q11381815}}* states that Funatama Shrine, a subsidiary shrine of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|de|Sumiyoshi-Taisha|es|Sumiyoshi Taisha|fa|سومییوشی-تایشا|fi|Sumiyoshi-taisha|fr|Sumiyoshi-taisha|it|Grande santuario di Sumiyoshi|ja|住吉大社|ko|스미요시 대사|la|Sumiyoshi-taisha|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနန်းကွန်းနန်းရင်း|pt|Sumiyoshi taisha|ru|Сумиёси-тайся|sl|Veliko svetišče Sumijoši-taiša|th|ศาลเจ้าซูมิโยชิ|tr|Sumiyoshi-taisha|uk|Сумійосі тайся|zh|住吉大社|qid=Q705949}}, was the clan deity of the Ki clan and the main shrine of “Shima Shrine, Shizuhi Shrine, and Date Shrine.”

== History ==
== Founding ==
The date of founding is unknown. == Overview ==
In the national histories, together with Date Shrine and Shima Shrine (Shima Jinja), Shizuhi Shrine is recorded as having received promotions in divine rank: from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade in {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|de|Jōwa|es|Jōwa (período Heian)|fa|جووا (دوره هی‌آن)|fr|Ère Jōwa (Heian)|ia|Jowa|id|Jōwa|ja|承和 (日本)|ko|조와 (834년)|ru|Дзёва (Хэйан)|simple|Jōwa (Heian period)|sr|Џова (Хејан период)|tr|Jōwa (Heian)|uk|Дзьова (ненґо)|zh|承和 (日本)|zh_yue|承和|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 11 ({{ill|844|ab|844|af|844|als|844|am|844 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|844|ar|844|ary|844|ast|844|avk|844|az|844|azb|۸۴۴ (میلادی)|bcl|844|be|844|be_x_old|844|bg|844|bn|৮৪৪|bpy|মারি ৮৪৪|br|844|bs|844.|ca|844|cdo|844 nièng|ceb|844|ckb|٨٤٤|crh|844|cs|844|csb|844|cv|844|cy|844|da|844|de|844|el|844|eml|844|eo|844|es|844|et|844|eu|844|fa|۸۴۴ (میلادی)|fi|844|fo|844|fr|844|frr|844|fy|844|ga|844|gan|844年|gd|844|gl|844|he|844|hi|844|hr|844.|ht|844 (almanak jilyen)|hu|844|hy|844|id|844|ilo|844|io|844|it|844|ja|844年|jv|844|ka|844|kaa|844|kk|844 жыл|ko|844년|la|844|lb|844|lij|844|lmo|844|lt|844 m.|lv|844. gads|map_bms|844|mdf|844|mg|844|mhr|844|mk|844|mr|इ.स. ८४४|mrj|844 и|ms|844|mzn|۸۴۴|nah|844|nap|844|nds|844|new|सन् ८४४|nl|844|nn|844|no|844|nrm|844|nso|844|oc|844|or|୮୪୪|os|844-æм аз|pl|844|pnb|844|pt|844|qu|844|ro|844|ru|844 год|rue|844|sa|८४४|scn|844|sd|844ع|se|844|sh|844.|shn|844|si|844|simple|844|sk|844|sl|844|smn|844|sq|844|sr|844|su|844|sv|844|sw|844|tg|Соли 844|th|พ.ศ. 1387|tk|844|tl|844|tly|844|tr|844|tt|844 ел|uk|844|ur|844ء|uz|844|vec|844|vi|844|vls|844|war|844|wuu|844年|xmf|844|zh|844年|zh_min_nan|844 nî|zh_yue|844年|qid=Q23835}}); In the *{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}* *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}*, it is listed under {{ill|Kii Province|cs|Provincie Kii|de|Provinz Kii|es|Provincia de Kii|eu|Kii probintzia|fa|ولایت کیئی|fr|Province de Kii|gl|Provincia de Kii|id|Provinsi Kii|it|Kii (provincia)|ja|紀伊国|ko|기이국|lt|Kijo žemė|nl|Kii (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Kii|pt|Província de Kii|ru|Кии (провинция)|simple|Kii Province|sk|Kii (provincia)|sr|Провинција Киј|th|แคว้นคิอิ|tr|Kii (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кії|vi|Tỉnh Kii|zh|紀伊國|zh_min_nan|Kii-kok|qid=Q864053}}{{ill|Nagusa district|ja|名草郡|zh|名草郡|qid=Q11415547}} as “Shizuhi Shrine, Myōjin Grand Shrine,” placing it among the {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}; the *{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|ja|紀伊国神名帳|qid=Q17210008}}* records it as “Senior First Rank, Shizuhi Ōkami” {{Sfn|Shizuhi Shrine Site (Heibonsha)|1983|p=376}}. In all cases, it is ranked higher than Kamayama Shrine.

It is said that together with {{ill|Itate Shrine|ja|伊達神社 (和歌山市)|qid=Q11380847|lt=Date Shrine}} (Sonobe, Wakayama City) and {{ill|Shima Shrine|ja|志磨神社|zh|志磨神社|qid=Q17212913}} ({{ill|Nakanoshima|ja|中之島 (和歌山市)|qid=Q17226981|lt=Nakanoshima}}, Wakayama City), it was known as the “Ki Sansho-sha” {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=362}}. According to the *{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|ja|住吉大社神代記|qid=Q11381815}}*, the origin of the Ki Sansho-sha lies in the three ships used by {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس جینگو|fr|Jingū|hr|Jingū (japanska carica)|hu|Dzsingú japán császárnő|id|Permaisuri Jingū|it|Jingū|ja|神功皇后|ka|ძინგუ|ko|진구 황후|nl|Jingu|pl|Jingū|pt|Jingu|ru|Императрица Дзингу|sh|Carica Jingū|si|ජින්ගූ අධිරාජිනිය|simple|Empress Jingū|sl|Cesarica Džingu|sv|Jingu Kogo|te|రాణి జింగూ|th|จักรพรรดินีจิงงู|tl|Emperatris Jingū|tr|Jingū (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Дзінґу|uz|Imperator Jingū|vi|Thiên hoàng Jingū|zh|神功皇后|zh_min_nan|Sîn-kong Hông-hō͘|zh_yue|神功皇后|qid=Q232803}} for the {{ill|Three Han Campaign|ja|三韓征伐|ko|삼한 정벌|zh|三韩征伐|qid=Q11249435}}, which she had {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|de|Takenouchi no Sukune|es|Takenouchi no Sukune|fa|تاکنوشی نو سوکون|fr|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰|ko|다케우치노 스쿠네|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯅꯣꯎꯆꯤ ꯅꯣ ꯁꯨꯀꯨꯅꯦ|pt|Takenouchi no Sukune|zh|武內宿禰|qid=Q1073668}} enshrine {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983|p=362}}.

Furthermore, since Wada Village was formerly a shrine estate of {{ill|Hinokuma Shrine|ja|日前神宮・國懸神宮|simple|Hinokuma Jingū|zh|日前宮|qid=Q888184}}, the deity of Shizuhi was closely connected with those shrines and with the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|fr|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀伊国造|simple|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qid=Q11604953|lt=hereditary governors of Kii Province}}. At Kusa-no-miya, enshrined within the grounds of those shrines, it is said that on September 15 the deity of Shizuhi made a sacred procession and the Shizuhi Festival was held {{Sfn|Kamayama Shrine and Shizuhi Shrine (Kami-gami)|1986|pp=316–318}}.
